record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.context_brief: Covering a unit cube by smaller cubes
record.original_question: For n >= 3, determine q(n), the minimum number of cubes in R^n, each with edge length smaller than 1 and not necessarily parallel to the covered cube, whose union contains a unit cube.

evidence.quote: Question 7. What is the minimum number q(n) of cubes in Rn of edge length smaller than 1 whose union contains a unit cube?
It is not difficult to prove that q(2) = 3 and that q(n) >= n + 1 for every n, but the exact value of q(n) has not yet been established for any n >= 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For an integer $n \geq 3$, let $q(n)$ denote the minimum number of $n$-dimensional cubes in $\mathbb{R}^n$, each of edge length strictly less than $1$ and arbitrarily oriented (not required to be axis-aligned or parallel to the unit cube), whose union contains a closed unit cube $[0,1]^n$. Determine the exact value of $q(n)$ for every $n \geq 3$. It is known that $q(2)=3$ and $q(n)\geq n+1$ for all $n\geq 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found establishing the exact value of q(n) for any n ≥ 3. The known bounds (q(2)=3 and q(n) ≥ n+1) are the only confirmed facts; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Covering a square by congruent squares
status_evidence.snippet: Studies covering problems for squares/cubes by smaller copies; the higher-dimensional analogue remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Related covering problem; exact value for n≥3 not established.
